text: Users can switch between a plain terminal view and a dedicated multi-turn agent conversation view
quote: Switch between a clean terminal for commands and a dedicated conversation view for multi-turn agent workflows.

text: Warp can run third-party CLI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) with rich input, review and notifications
quote: Run third-party CLI agents like Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode with the agent toolbelt — rich input, code review, notifications, and more.

text: An official `warp` command starts an agent conversation in any terminal, including over SSH or on machines without Warp installed
quote: Run the `warp` command to start a conversation in whichever terminal you already use, over SSH, or on a machine where Warp isn’t installed.

text: Automations can be triggered by events from Slack, Linear, GitHub or custom webhooks
quote: Triggers: React to events from Slack, Linear, GitHub, or custom webhooks

text: Recurring tasks (e.g. dependency updates, dead code removal) can be scheduled to run automatically
quote: Schedules: Run recurring tasks like dependency updates or dead code removal

text: A built-in agent can write code, run commands, and iterate autonomously until a described task is complete
quote: Describe what you want to build and let Warp's built‑in agent handle the rest — writing code, running commands, and iterating until the task is done.

text: Warp AI can connect to external tools/data (databases, APIs, docs, internal services) via the Model Context Protocol
quote: Connect Warp AI to any tool via the Model Context Protocol. Pull context from databases, APIs, docs, and internal services so the AI understands your full stack.

text: Typing '#' followed by a natural-language description generates the matching shell command in real time
quote: Type '#' on your command line and start describing the command you want to run using natural language. Warp will load AI Command Suggestions as you type.

text: Right-click 'Ask Warp AI' explains command errors and identifies missing dependencies
quote: Right‑click and 'Ask Warp AI' to explain any error in your command output.

text: Warp supports multiple AI models (Claude Sonnet/Opus, GPT, Gemini) with automatic routing to the best model for a task
quote: Warp supports Claude Sonnet and Opus, GPT, and Gemini Pro — and adds new models as they launch. Pick the model that fits your task, or let Warp route automatically.

text: Users can save workflows in Warp Drive to run on-demand or share with a team, with AI assisting naming/parameterizing
quote: Warp lets you save your most important workflows in Warp Drive so you can run them on‑demand or share with your team. Let Warp AI handle the hard part of naming, describing, and parameterizing the command.

text: Warp prevents OpenAI/Anthropic from using user data for model training and never stores terminal input/output on its servers
quote: Warp does not allow OpenAI or Anthropic to use your data for model training. Our "hands off" approach also means your terminal input and output data is never stored on Warp servers.

text: The agent can drive long-running or full-screen interactive terminal apps (e.g. sqlite, python), providing input and navigating screens
quote: the Warp Agent can now run and control long-running or full-screen terminal applications. The agent can provide input when prompted, navigate interactive screens, and continue execution without stalling.

text: A native Network Log lets users monitor telemetry in real time and opt out at any time
quote: Monitor telemetry in real-time with Warp’s native Network Log. Opt out of telemetry at any time

text: Themes can be auto-generated from a background image
quote: Automatically create new themes based on a background image.

text: Theme can automatically sync with the OS's light/dark mode setting
quote: Warp supports synchronizing your theme with the OS’s light and dark themes.

text: Windows, tabs, panes, and recent Blocks are automatically restored when Warp relaunches
quote: Restore your windows, tabs, panes, and recent Blocks automatically when you relaunch Warp.

text: The Oz CLI runs and manages Warp's cloud agents from any terminal, script, or CI pipeline, including connecting MCP servers and integrations
quote: The Oz CLI is the command-line tool for running and managing Warp’s cloud agents from any terminal, script, or CI pipeline. Use it to start agents locally or in the cloud, connect MCP servers, configure integrations, and authenticate withou

text: The Warp Agent CLI can switch directories mid-session and run agents on remote machines without installing remote binaries
quote: The Warp Agent CLI lets you switch directories while in an agent session, and even run agents on remote machines without installing remote binaries.

text: Warp's client source code is publicly readable/auditable under the AGPL v3 open-source license
quote: Read and audit Warp’s client source code at warpdotdev/warp, open source under AGPL v3

text: Telemetry must remain enabled to use AI features on the Free plan, but paid plans can opt out anytime and keep using AI
quote: Telemetry must be enabled to use AI features on the Free plan, while paid plans can opt out at any time and continue using Warp, including AI.

text: Business/Enterprise plans have a Zero Data Retention agreement guaranteeing no AI interaction or console data is collected
quote: Business and Enterprise plans are covered by our Zero Data Retention (ZDR) agreement. No AI interaction or console data is ever collected.

text: Users can mark sensitive Blocks to prevent local saving, or clear Blocks from a machine entirely
quote: Sometimes, you may want to prevent a sensitive Block from being saved on your computer, or you may want to clear blocks from a machine entirely.

text: A settings file gives users and agents programmatic control over configuration and easy portability between devices
quote: we are shipping a (long-overdue) settings file so that users and agents get programmatic control over settings and easy portability between devices.

text: The Warp Agent is available as a standalone CLI usable inside other terminals and IDEs (Ghostty, iTerm2, VS Code, built-in terminals)
quote: The Warp Agent is now available as a standalone CLI that you can use anywhere – Ghostty, iTerm 2, VS Code, built-in Windows and Mac Terminals

text: Warp is built as a platform exposing API, CLI, SDK, and MCP interfaces rather than a single vertical product
quote: API, CLI, SDK and MCP built as a platform, not a vertical product or AI teammate.

text: Secret Redaction is unconditionally applied to all AI interactions so sensitive data is never collected or sent to third parties
quote: Warp unconditionally applies Secret Redaction in all AI interactions to ensure that any sensitive data is _never_ collected or sent to third parties.

text: Every agent run is tracked, auditable, and shareable with a team
quote: Observability: Every run is tracked, auditable, and shareable with your team

text: Agent runs can be watched, steered, and handed off across web, mobile, terminal, or IDE surfaces
quote: any surface — watch, steer, and hand off runs from web, mobile, terminal, or IDE.

text: Many agents can be run concurrently across different repos or tasks
quote: Parallelism: Run many agents concurrently across repos or tasks
